properties.state: {"decision":"UNDECIDED. Anthony, 2026-07-25: COORD.md was invented so he and his brother could coordinate; the claims layer shipped the same day; and reflow2 is developed by using reflow2 on itself, so the question is whether the markdown board should now be a graph read. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE, because it is less than it sounds: `claim_region` records a Contributor holding a seed node to a depth, `claim_report` computes the region and the overlaps, and both travel in the committed export exactly as COORD.md travels in git — so visibility is unchanged, and the gain is that the region is COMPUTED from the design (it follows the graph as the design moves) rather than being a hand-typed list of file paths that goes stale silently. WHAT WOULD BE LOST, and it is the part worth deciding rather than assuming: COORD.md is readable by a human with no reflow2 and no binary, it shows up as a diff in a pull request, and it holds the merge-conflict doctrine for the shared records — none of which a graph read does. The sane split, if this is taken: claims in the graph for WHO HAS WHAT, COORD.md retained for the conventions and the conflict doctrine, and the in-progress table deleted rather than maintained in two places, since two places for the same fact is the failure the backlog-in-the-graph move exists to end.","name":"OPEN — does reflow2's own claim board move from COORD.md into the graph?","rationale":"Raised as a dogfooding question, which is how most of this project's real findings have arrived — and it is a genuinely good test of the claims layer, because reflow2's own two-person collaboration is the only live multi-writer case that exists. Held proposed because a claim board is a coordination mechanism between two people, and switching it unilaterally would mean one of them silently changing where the other must look; that is Anthony's brother's call as much as his. The prerequisite is honest: nobody has used claim_region for real yet, so the first move is to run it on one real piece of work and see whether claim_report says something a person would have said.","status":"proposed"}
